content.text: {"candidates":[{"id":"E13","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6","Q5"],"candidate_type":"combined","title":"Medium-normalized TEA vs TEOA","purpose":"Test whether a TEA/TEOA selectivity difference persists after tighter matching of solvent and proton-delivery conditions in P01 rather than only nominal donor substitution. If the CO/H2 contrast contracts under normalized composition, that supports a medium/proton-management contribution without proving the detailed cause.","method":"Run the matched P01 benchmark with TEA and TEOA while explicitly holding MeCN/H2O ratio, total amine-derived volume fraction, CO2 handling, cobalt/bpy/g-C3N4 loadings, and analysis fixed; compare CO, H2, and CO/H2 time profiles across the donor pair under the original and composition-normalized settings.","evidence_ids":["EV061","EV013","GX009","EV059","EV031"],"distinct_information":"This is the key comparative intervention for H03 because it asks whether donor identity effects survive stronger control of variables linked in the literature to proton supply, dissolved CO2, viscosity, and local medium. It discriminates medium-coupled association from a donor effect that remains robust after normalization.","dependencies":["E01","E02"]},{"id":"E14","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6","Q4"],"candidate_type":"characterization","title":"Isotope-sensitive operando signatures","purpose":"Ask whether TEA and TEOA produce different H/D-sensitive spectroscopic features under CO2 reduction conditions, consistent with different hydrogen-containing or proton-coupled states. A donor-dependent isotope response would support, but not uniquely assign, a proton-management explanation.","method":"Acquire operando or near-operando IR and/or complementary spectroscopy on matched P01 TEA and TEOA samples under CO2 with H2O versus D2O substitution, using donor-free and dark references where feasible and treating peak assignments as provisional unless isotope shifts and controls agree.","evidence_ids":["EV080","GX010","GX015","EV031"],"distinct_information":"This characterization targets the discriminating prediction that the donor effect should track isotope-sensitive observables if proton delivery or hydrogen-containing intermediates differ. It cannot by itself exclude cobalt-state or donor-redox differences if several processes shift together.","dependencies":["E13"]},{"id":"E15","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6"],"candidate_type":"characterization","title":"CO2-associated donor speciation","purpose":"Determine whether TEA and TEOA generate different CO2-associated solution states before or during illumination, such as amine-CO2 or donor-linked adduct signatures, under otherwise matched P01 medium. Detectable donor-specific CO2-associated signals would support a local substrate-environment contribution.","method":"Measure donor-containing P01 media with and without CO2 saturation, before illumination and under reaction-relevant equilibration, using solution IR and/or NMR style readouts transferable for CO2-associated speciation; compare TEA, TEOA, and no-amine references while keeping solvent composition fixed.","evidence_ids":["EV029","EV061","GX009","EV031"],"distinct_information":"This descriptive experiment addresses whether the donors differ in substrate-associated chemistry rather than only electron donation. Positive differences would still be associational unless later linked to catalytic output under the same matched conditions.","dependencies":["E13"]},{"id":"E16","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6","Q1"],"candidate_type":"intervention","title":"Amine omission and inert-base replacement","purpose":"Separate amine necessity from amine specificity by testing whether product formation requires the donor/additive and whether a non-donor pH/base adjustment can mimic part of the TEA/TEOA effect. This distinguishes omission from substitution and bounds how much of the donor effect could reflect bulk basicity alone.","method":"In the P01 assay, compare full TEA and TEOA runs to no-amine controls and to conditions where an added non-sacrificial base or proton-balancing adjustment is introduced without replacing the donor role; quantify CO and H2 with the same workflow and interpret only bounded descriptive rescue or non-rescue outcomes.","evidence_ids":["EV013","EV024","GX010","GX015","GX008"],"distinct_information":"No-amine tests necessity, whereas inert-base replacement tests whether proton-management or base environment can partially substitute for donor identity; these answer different questions. Because a non-donor base cannot replicate reductive quenching, any partial rescue would support a mixed-function explanation rather than full equivalence.","dependencies":["E01","E02"]},{"id":"E17","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6","Q5"],"candidate_type":"combined","title":"Water-fraction crossover map","purpose":"Test whether the TEA/TEOA selectivity contrast depends strongly on water content, as expected if proton availability and local medium govern the observed donor effect. A crossover or collapse across water fraction would favor H03 over a donor-identity effect that is largely water-insensitive.","method":"For each donor in P01, vary only the MeCN/H2O composition around the baseline while holding catalyst, ligand, g-C3N4, nominal donor condition, CO2 handling, and illumination fixed; collect CO and H2 outputs together and, where possible, paired medium descriptors such as pH/pD or conductivity.","evidence_ids":["GX009","EV061","EV013","EV031"],"distinct_information":"This is a comparative medium intervention rather than a donor-amount series, designed to reveal whether donor identity interacts with proton-source richness or solvent environment. It is especially informative if TEA and TEOA differ at one water fraction but converge at another.","dependencies":["E13"]},{"id":"E18","hypothesis_id":"H03","question_ids":["Q6","Q5"],"candidate_type":"combined","title":"Proton-readout correlation set","purpose":"Link donor-dependent catalytic selectivity to directly measured medium/proton-related covariates rather than inferring them from composition alone. Correlation of CO/H2 shifts with donor-dependent pH/pD, conductivity, or related bulk descriptors would support H03 but remain non-causal without the matched interventions.","method":"On the same TEA and TEOA formulations used for catalytic comparisons, record pre- and post-irradiation bulk medium descriptors accessible in P01, such as pH or pD proxies, conductivity, and gas uptake-relevant equilibration measures, then compare their direction of change with CO and H2 outputs.","evidence_ids":["GX009","EV061","GX010","EV013"],"distinct_information":"This adds bounded descriptive measurements that can explain whether TEA and TEOA actually create different proton-management environments under matched nominal recipes. It cannot identify the microscopic intermediate, but it helps interpret whether later isotope or substitution results are plausibly medium-driven.","dependencies":["E13"]}],"gaps":["No supplied evidence gives a strict within-paper TEA-versus-TEOA head-to-head in the exact P01 recipe, so H03 experiments remain transfer-based until the matched benchmark is confirmed.","The supplied evidence supports proton-management and CO2-association as plausible explanations, but direct TEA/TEOA observation of specific amine-CO2 adducts in a Co-bpy photocatalytic system is absent.","Quantitative pKa, dissolved-CO2, viscosity, and conductivity values for the exact target media are not provided here, so normalization variables may need pilot verification before strong inference.","No direct source evidence here establishes which operando spectral features should be assigned to cobalt-bound versus donor- or solvent-derived intermediates in P01, so assignments may remain ambiguous even with isotope controls.","Identity substitution beyond TEA and TEOA is not strongly evidenced for this exact Co-bpy platform, so broader donor-scope conclusions should be deferred."]}
